storyboarding_game:
The goal of the game is to build stories using scenes & characters they build - based on the
cues they get with dice rolls & card draws.

Players will paint the character cards and the scenes , then arrange the scenes into a story.

Step 1 : Roll 8 sided planet dice ( needs 0pt in 1st round & 30pts in subsequent rounds to roll)

Step 2: Roll 12 sided Region dice (needs 0pt in 1st round & 20pts in subsequent rounds to roll)

Step 3: Draw A Being Card from a set of 30 Being cards

Step 4 : Choose To Draw A Character Card or
Pay 25pts to Roll Setting Dice & or Pay 50pts to Roll Powers & Disabilities Dice & then Draw A
Character Card.

Step 5 : If the Character Card is Blank, Design a Character with the being, region & planet cues
drawn & earn 50pts.
If the Character Card is already designed one, keep it & move on.

Step 6 : Draw A Scene Card ( needs 0 pt is drawn right after drawing a character card & needs
35 pts if not after a character card).
If the Scene Card is already filled keep it and move on to step 9)

Step 7 : If scene Card is Blank, Draw a Cue Card.

Step 8 : Paint the Scene Card using the character drawn/designed , & the cue card for the
scene & all the settings drawn.

Step 9: continue with the next round, either start from drawing a being card for free, designing a
character & following the the same flow. Or choose to skip character design part and pay for a
scene Card to design another scene for the same character, and same settings.
You can also choose to pay and roll Planet & Region dices for character design or use the same
ones drawn before.

Goal : is to keep going in rounds until you can arrange the scenes into a story. Any story , any
length , etc. but a story.

2+ people - split into teams, they continue as long as one team submits their story , at which
point the other team must also submit their story.

Completing a story earns 50pts
 All enjoy the story and score 1-5 on the following

1. Shortest 2. Longest 3. Funniest 4. Saddest 5. Trippiest 6. Randomest 7. Most artistic 8. Least
artistic 9. Deepest 10. Silliest 11. Most detailed 12. Least detailed.

A story can be given an excellence award under one or more of the above categories which will
earn the story and the players involved 75 pts. There can be 0-1 excellence award per game.

These scores on different criteria will be added on every time they play the game. If I'm playing
solo, my points will increase. If 2 people are on a team, both will get the same score of the
story. When I'm playing solo, I finish the story and send it to other players for scoring.

For every first 10 marks on each category, the player gets 25 pts that can be used in the game.

After that every 50 in each category earns the player(s) 20pts.

Game Hardware:

1. Planet Dice (8 sided)- Earth, Mars, Venus, YYY, ZZZ, BBB, DDD, Custom

2. Region Dice (12 sided)- Ocean, Tropical Land, Desert Land, Beach Side, City, Village,
Industrial/Tech Centers, Forest, Ice Land, Mountain, FarmLand, Custom

3. Beings Cards - Fish, Canis, Felis, Reptilian, Bacteria, Octopus, Whale, Bonobo, Human,
Virus, Elephant, Ants, Turtles/Tortoise, Plants, Trees, Dinos& Birds, Fungi, Bish (bird+ fish),
Deagle(dog+ eagle), custom (blank) - 11.

4. Setting Dice (8 sided) - Tornado, Tsunami, Golden Period, Revolution, Post Apocalypse,
Capitalism, communism, poverty& plague.

5. Powers & Disabilities Dice - Spit Fire, Hug & Cure, Fly Fast, Oneness, No Movement, No
sight

6. Scene Cue Cards - Epiphany, Ego Clash, Love, Emotional, Death, Birth, Friendship, Conflict,
Dream, Random, Funny, Metaphysical, Hunger, Help, custom

7. Shot Cards -
 8. Hurdle Cards - draw, play with it & get 2x points - 2 min time limit, upside down, single stroke,
2 colour scheme, etc

9.

Character Cards - All Blank - 100

Scene Cards - All Blank - 500

Modes :

 1. Fixed turns mode
 2. Race
 3. Collaborative Epic
 4. Slow Masterpiece

Other Gameplays

 1. Random cue card draws, players draw scenes, producer puts together a story

game_types_universe:
🕹 Universal Game Types / Formats
🎲 A. Chance & Randomness
Dice / Spinners / Coins → randomize outcomes.
Draw-from-Deck → unknown card creates suspense.
Lottery / Raffle → win by chance.
Push-Your-Luck → risk vs reward, stop or continue.
🧩 B. Puzzle & Problem Solving
Jigsaw Assembly → piece-to-picture.
Pattern Recognition → sequence, logic, visual.
Escape Room / Clue Chains → solve step by step.
Hidden Objects / Spot the Difference.
Riddles / Lateral Thinking Challenges.
🎯 C. Collection & Matching
Memory Flip → pair finding.
Domino Chains → match ends.
Set Building → collect 3 of a kind, complete families.
Trading/Swapping → barter system.
Bingo → match drawn items to board.
🚶 D. Movement & Embodied Play
Relay Races → pass objects, timed.
Obstacle Course → crawl, climb, balance.
Dance / Freeze Games.
Simon Says / Copycat.
Scavenger Hunt → find, fetch, collect.
Human Domino / Chain Reaction.
🧑‍🤝‍🧑 E. Social Role & Simulation
Roleplay / Pretend → kids embody characters.
Charades / Acting Guess.
Tableau → freeze into shapes/scenes.
Role Swap → kid as teacher/parent.
Debate / Judge & Jury.
Market Simulation → trade, buy, sell.
🎭 F. Story & Narrative
Reading Stories, Writing Stories
Story Dice / Story Cards.
Build-a-Story Chain → each adds a sentence.
Choose Your Path → branching decisions.
Mystery / Detective Games.
Adventure Quests → missions, journeys.
Puppet/Mask Theatre.
🎨 G. Creative Expression
Drawing Prompts → doodle then guess.
Collaborative Drawing → pass paper.
Painting Challenges → interpret music/emotion.
Build / Sculpt / Craft as Play.
Dance Improvisation.
Music-Making → rhythm circles, soundscapes.
🧠 H. Strategy & Tactics
Board Strategy → capture territory, outsmart opponent.
Resource Management → limited tokens, spend wisely.
Planning Ahead → chess-like, predict moves.
Bluffing / Hidden Info → “Werewolf”-style games.
Co-op Strategy → group beats a system.
🔄 I. Transformation & Manipulation
Break & Rebuild → entropy, Legos, clay.
Combination Games → mix two things into third.
Mutation/Variation → tweak rules or pieces.
Before/After Transformations → reveal what changes.
🕵️ J. Information & Knowledge Games
Trivia / Quiz Style.
Guess Who / Deduction Games.
20 Questions.
Sorting/Classifying Challenges.
Detective Work → “find the cause.”
📱 K. Digital-Light Mechanics (Optional)
Timers / Beat the Clock.
QR Treasure Hunt.
AR Peek / Pop-up Clues.
Stop-Motion Animation.
Digital Pictionary / Drawing Board.
🎮 The Big Gameplay Library (for Kids ~6+)
🎲 1. Card-Based Play
Draw & Do → instruction card.
Matching → pairs, memory flip.
Sorting → by category, property.

🔬 1. Experiments-as-Play
(Drop a ball, burn paper with a lens, grow crystals)
Falls under Puzzle & Problem-Solving (kids predict → test → see feedback).
Also under Exploration / Simulation → you’re simulating physics or natural laws.
👉 Key mechanic = hypothesis + test + observe.
So in taxonomy: Experiments = Problem-Solving + Simulation mechanics.
🤸 2. Activities / Embodied Challenges
(Run around house, jump, relay, freeze dance)
Already under Movement & Embodied Play.
Key mechanic = body as tool.
👉 Often overlaps with Sports/Game mechanics (competition, time, scoring).
🏏 3. Sports & Games (Chess, Cricket, etc.) as Cross-Learning
These map into classic Strategy / Competition mechanics:
Chess → Strategy, Planning Ahead, Pattern Recognition.
Cricket / Football → Teamwork, Roleplay (batsman/bowler/goalkeeper), Probability (coin toss, outcomes), Physics (forces, angles).
Racing games → Time pressure, Optimization.
👉 Sports add team, score, and time layers that pure experiments often lack.
🗺 4. Exploration / Outdoor Play
(Treasure hunts, map quests, scavenger challenges)
Taxonomy: Exploration mechanics.
Different from experiments: no “lab result,” instead discovery, searching, spatial reasoning.
🧪 5. “Run-Your-Own Lab” Games
Parent sets rules → kid tweaks variables (drop ball on sand vs floor, change height, change shape).
That’s Rule Variation mechanics → turning science into iterative play.
🕹 Extended Gameplay Categories (to cover your cases)
In addition to Cards / Boards / Dice / Puzzles / Roleplay / Art / Music / Theatre, we must also explicitly include:
Experimentation Games → Predict → Test → Observe → Reflect.
Embodied / Physical Activity Games → Body is tool (run, jump, act).
Sports Mechanics → Team, competition, scoring, time.
Exploration / Quest Games → Hunt, discover, map.
Rule Variation Games → tweak variables to explore outcomes.
🔬 Science Experiments as Gameplay Types
1. Predict–Test–Observe (Core Experiment Play)
Setup → ask kid to predict outcome.
Run experiment → compare result.
Example: Drop a feather vs a ball → which lands first?
👉 This is the “Guess & Reveal” mechanic, same as drawing a mystery card, but in real world.
2. Variable-Changing Experiments (Rule Variation Play)
Repeat with 1 change (height, size, material).
Kids compare results.
Example: Bounce different balls from same height → which bounces higher?
👉 Same structure as “tweak rules in a board game” → teaches systems thinking.
3. Cause & Effect Chains (Experiment as Domino)
One event triggers another.
Example: Vinegar + baking soda → gas → blows up balloon.
Treat as chain-reaction game (like Rube Goldberg).
👉 Mechanic = “Trigger something and see cascade.”
4. Exploration Experiments (Discovery Play)
Open-ended, no set “right” answer.
Example: Shine flashlight on objects → what shadows/shapes appear?
Mechanic = Exploration / Mapping.
5. Competition Experiments (Challenge Play)
Time it, measure it, race it.
Example: Whose paper airplane flies farthest?
Mechanic = Sports overlay on science.
6. Simulation Experiments (Model Play)
Use simple objects to model big systems.
Example: Bed sheet + balls → spacetime curvature.
Mechanic = Roleplay but with objects.

game_play_components:
🕹 Parts of Gameplay (for DeepKids)
1. Hook (Entry Point)
Something that makes the kid lean in: surprise, mystery, challenge, or silliness.
Can be: a question (“Can you make this circle look like a ball?”), a card drawn, a funny prop, a mystery bag.
👉 Without a hook, the kid never cares enough to begin.
2. Goal (Why we play)
Clear outcome: “build the tallest tower,” “make the picture look real,” “uncover the hidden rule.”
Goals can be win/lose, discover, or explore.
👉 Without a goal, play feels like aimless activity.
3. Rules & Constraints (The Frame)
Define what’s allowed/not allowed.
E.g., “only 1 minute,” “only these 3 colors,” “no talking.”
👉 Rules create tension → tension creates thinking.
4. Actions / Mechanics (The Doing)
The verbs of play: roll, draw, paint, guess, act, build, break.
Kids learn through the doing, not the instructions.
👉 Rich mechanics = richer thought.
5. Feedback (Response Loop)
Immediate signals: the tower falls, the dice shows 6, the shadow looks real.
Feedback shows the consequence of choices → fuels curiosity.
👉 Without feedback, no learning sticks.
6. Progression (Sense of Journey)
Levels, increasing challenges, variations, or surprises.
Can be narrative (“Now the sun moves!”), or difficulty (“Try with 2 light sources”).
👉 Keeps engagement alive past the first 2 minutes.
7. Reflection (Pause & Think)
Questions: “Why did this happen? What did you notice? What if we changed ___?”
Can be guided by parent cards, peer sharing, or just journaling.
👉 This is where deep learning emerges from raw play.
8. Social / Collaborative Layer (Optional but Powerful)
Roles (one paints, one guesses the light source).
Sharing outcomes (compare spheres, debate why shadows differ).
Co-op goals (“together draw the solar system with shadows”).
👉 Builds curiosity + questioning via interaction.
9. Meaning / Connection (Why it Matters)
Tie to bigger picture: “Artists use this trick,” “Our eyes see light this way,” “Planets look round because of light and shadow.”
👉 Prevents game from being “just fun,” anchors it in knowledge/insight.
10. Closure (Ending / Takeaway)
Wrap-up: a solved puzzle, a finished drawing, a shared laugh.
Optional meta: “What did we discover today?”
👉 Gives a sense of completion — kid feels they actually did something.
🧩 Extended Anatomy of Gameplay
11. Onboarding (How kids enter without friction)
Clear, simple start. Kids don’t like 10-minute rule explanations.
Needs an easy first step that pulls them in before they know all the rules.
👉 “Pick a card and do what it says” is instant onboarding.
12. Autonomy (Choice & Agency)
Give kids a decision → pick a card, choose a role, select the tool.
Agency = ownership = curiosity.
👉 Without choice, it feels like homework.
13. Surprise / Delight
Random events, unexpected twists, hidden reveals.
Keeps the brain on edge → fuels dopamine → keeps curiosity alive.
👉 A kit without surprise = a worksheet.
14. Replayability / Variability
Each playthrough should feel a little different.
Dice, random cards, or changeable setups give freshness.
👉 Prevents one-and-done boredom.
15. Identity / Role
Even if not full roleplay, kids love to “be something.”
Example: “You’re the Sun, I’m the Moon,” or “You’re the Entropy Monster scattering beads.”
👉 Identity makes abstract concepts visceral.
16. Aesthetics / Immersion
Design matters: colors, tactile feel, playful names.
“Shadow Detective” is more engaging than “Shading Exercise.”
👉 Emotional engagement = deeper learning.
17. Scaffolded Difficulty (Stretch Zone)
Starts easy → gets harder.
Keeps flow state: not boring, not impossible.
👉 E.g., draw sphere with one light source → then try two → then moving sun.
18. Meta-Learning Prompts
Space for kids to ask their own questions.
Example: “What if the Sun were below? What if the ball was shiny?”
👉 This turns play into exploration, not just execution.
19. Parent/Facilitator Role
Clear but light: guiding questions, setting rules, not taking over.
Without facilitation, younger kids drift or miss reflection.
👉 Parent = co-player, not teacher.
20. Emotional Loop
Play isn’t just cognitive → it needs fun, tension, release.
Frustration (tower falls) → try again → success = joy.
👉 That emotional arc = glue for memory.
gameplay_archetypes:
🧰 Gameplay Archetypes to Rotate
Here’s a starter set — so each topic can land in a unique way:
Cycle / Relay Games
For concepts that are about flow, transformation, continuity.
Eg: Energy, Water Cycle, Food Chain.
Mystery / Detective Play
For concepts about hidden layers, cause-effect, investigation.
Eg: Causality/Karma, Atoms/Particles, Consciousness.
Contradiction / Paradox Games
For concepts that hold two opposite truths at once.
Eg: Reality (real/not real), Quantum Physics (particle/wave), Zero & Infinity.
Arena / Debate Play
For concepts about clashing forces, multiple viewpoints.
Eg: Fringe Science, Time Travel ethics, Consciousness as universal vs. human-only.
Performance / Embodiment Games
For concepts that need to be felt in the body.
Eg: Gravity (fall, jump, balance), Sound (vibrate, sing, echo).
Puzzle / Construction Games
For concepts about structure, order, emergence.
Eg: Symmetry, Crystals, DNA, Math patterns.
Exploration / Mapping Games
For concepts about scale, place, orientation.
Eg: Universe history, Maps of space, Wormholes.
Economy / Resource Games
For concepts about limits, conservation, trade-offs.
Eg: Entropy, Energy efficiency, Zero-sum.
Story / Narrative Chain
For concepts that unfold over time and sequence.
Eg: Evolution story, History of Science, Causality strings.
Hidden Role / Secret Information Games
For concepts where observation changes outcome.
Eg: Observer Effect, Entanglement, Illusion/Mask.
learning_modes:
🧠 Types of Learning / Modes / Processes
1. Sensory Modes (How information enters)
Visual → diagrams, colors, patterns, watching demos.
Auditory → stories, songs, rhythms, instructions.
Kinesthetic → movement, touch, physical manipulation.
Oral/Linguistic → speaking, discussing, storytelling.
Written → reading, note-taking, writing reflections.
Multi-sensory → combining 2+ channels (art + story + sound).
2. Cognitive Processes (What brain does with input)
Memorization → recall facts, names, steps.
Comprehension → understand meaning, restate.
Application → use knowledge in a new task.
Analysis → break into parts, find relationships.
Synthesis/Creation → combine to make something new.
Evaluation → judge, debate, critique.
👉 (These are Bloom’s levels, but simplified for kids).
3. Experiential Modes (Learning by Doing)
Exploration → try without instructions, see what happens.
Experimentation → structured trial and error.
Simulation → model bigger system (roleplay atom/planet).
Practice / Drill → repeat until mastery (typing, math facts).
Project-based → build something (poster, model, story).
Play-based → game as main medium.
Problem-based → solve challenge with constraints.
4. Social Modes (Learning with Others)
Imitation → copy peer/parent.
Discussion → talk through ideas.
Cooperation → build something together.
Competition → try to outdo peers (healthy rivalry).
Teaching Others → kid explains to sibling/parent → retention spikes.
5. Reflective Modes (Turning experience into insight)
Self-questioning → “Why did this happen?”
Comparison → noticing differences, similarities.
Prediction vs Outcome → testing intuition.
Metacognition → “How did I solve this?”
Journaling / Drawing reflections → capturing thoughts.
6. Creative & Expressive Processes
Artistic expression → drawing, music, dance, theater.
Storytelling → narrative framing.
Roleplay → embodying characters or forces.
Invention / Design Thinking → “How else can we do this?”
Improvisation → spontaneous creation.
7. Embodied / Emotional Learning
Emotional association → surprise, delight, frustration → memory sticks.
Identity connection → “I am the Sun / I am the Explorer.”
Awe & Wonder → encountering the vast (universe, infinity).
Failure & Retry → safe mistakes build resilience.
8. Inquiry-Based Processes (Core for DeepKids)
Questioning → asking own questions.
Hypothesizing → forming guesses.
Testing → experiment.
Interpreting → making sense of results.
Connecting → link to larger patterns.
Generalizing → “If it works here, maybe it works there too.”
9. Modes of Knowledge (What is being learned)
Conceptual → big ideas (gravity, entropy, story structure).
Procedural → “how to” (tie shoelaces, run experiment).
Experiential → “I saw/felt it happen.”
Metacognitive → “I know how I learn.”
Values/Ethical → fairness, teamwork, respect.
